issues.body:
Carrying round 3's residual finding forward, but DOWNGRADED to nit after re-analysis.

The two new rows at 1506-1511 inject a `refuse` callable, so they never take the `require is None` branch at 100-102. Round 3 called that an uncaught-mutant gap; on the evidence it is not. `_load_workflow_yaml()` is called unconditionally at module scope (line 108), so a mutant that removes `from yaml_dependency import require_yaml` leaves `require` as None, `require(...)` raises TypeError at IMPORT time, and the script dies before any self-test row runs. The mutant is killed — loudly, in every lane.

What genuinely remains is only a failure-SHAPE wart: `except (ImportError, RuntimeError)` does not include TypeError, so that death is an unhandled traceback rather than the structured `(None, exc)` path the docstring advertises the loader preserves. The live consumers at 477 and 1088 are unaffected either way — both raise AlarmError when `yaml is None`, so there is no fail-open here and nothing gate-relevant.

Not blocking; recording it so the next reader does not re-derive it.
issues.fix_hint:
Optional. Either widen the tuple to `except (ImportError, RuntimeError, TypeError) as exc:` so an un-set `require` also lands on the structured path, or add one row that drives the real default branch by making the genuine import fail:

    import sys as _sys
    _saved = _sys.modules.pop("yaml_dependency", None)
    _sys.modules["yaml_dependency"] = None  # forces ImportError on `from ... import`
    try:
        default_path = _load_workflow_yaml()
    finally:
        _sys.modules.pop("yaml_dependency", None)
        if _saved is not None:
            _sys.modules["yaml_dependency"] = _saved
    chk("yaml loader takes the structured path when the helper module itself cannot be imported",
        default_path[0] is None and isinstance(default_path[1], ImportError))
issues.title: TypeError is outside the loader's except tuple, so the `require is None` default path fails with an opaque traceback rather than the structured detector path

verdict.summary:
Round 3's blocker is fixed and the nit is gone; only a nit-level residual remains, so this is approvable.

BLOCKER RESOLVED. scripts/yaml_dependency.py:87 now spells the entrypoint `if len(sys.argv) == 2 and sys.argv[1] == "--self-test":`. I re-ran the exact discovery ERE from worker-live.sh:1043 against the file and it matches (third alternative: `sys\.argv\[[^]]+\][[:space:]]*==[[:space:]]*"--self-test"`, with the `^[[:space:]]*[^#].*` prefix satisfied by the leading `if`). So `_derive_full_selftest_suite` adds it to `suite`, the enrolled-entry arm at 1053-1057 is satisfied (selftest-suite.txt:65), the reverse advertising-but-unenrolled arm at 1059-1063 is satisfied, and pr-gate.yml's `print-selftest-suite` step no longer aborts. The redundant `import sys` in the `__main__` block is also gone.

Re-verified the rest independently rather than trusting round 3:
- Sparse-checkout audit is complete. All 10 sparse-checkout blocks (metrics.yml:192, backfill-provenance.yml:69, groom-sweep.yml:396/483/580/664/758, regate-sweep.yml:69, dispatch.yml:109/1582) — every block whose job executes a converted consumer gained `scripts/yaml_dependency.py`. dispatch.yml:1582 correctly omits it: that job runs only dispatch-secrets-guard.py, which reads worker-pr.py via `ast` (dispatch-claim/guard:1419) and worker-live.sh as text, never importing either. backfill-provenance.yml:69 is the `resolve` job (tomllib heredoc); `backfill-provenance.py --self-test` runs at line 174 under the FULL checkout at line 123. Every other converted consumer's self-test runs under a full checkout.
- REQUIRED_FILES additions line up one-for-one with the corresponding sparse-checkouts (the assertions are `REQUIRED_FILES ⊆ sparse_lines`, e.g. ci-latency-alert.py:2929-2931), so no side reds.
